name: Abū Muḥriz Khalaf ibn Ḥayyān, known as Khalaf al-Aḥmar
summary: Basran transmitter of the old poetry, client of Abū Burda, whose own verses in the ancient manner could not be told from the old poets'; teacher of al-Aṣmaʿī and Abū Nuwās.
bio: Khalaf was a client of Abū Burda ibn Abī Mūsā, who had freed his parents, both from Farghāna. Ibn al-Anbārī says he composed poetry so well in the manner of the ancient poets that what he ascribed to them could not be told apart from their own.
Al-Zubaydī counts him in the third generation of the lexicographers of Basra.
uncertain: Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of death; TDV gives about 180/796.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 69–71
